title: The power of smell
paragraphs: Have you ever caught a whiff of something and been strongly reminded of a person or place? It seems there is a deep psychological link between smells, our personality and our memory. Some research even suggests that smells can influence our cognition.

So, why do smells take us back? Roja Dove, a perfumer, told the BBC that when we are born, the olfactory bulb, which is the area in our brain that processes smell, is empty. Therefore, our responses to smell are learnt and very personal to the individual. This means that when we smell an odour again, the original and unique memory comes flooding back because of the association.

Our awareness of smells is primarily unconscious, according to Andreas Keller from the Department of Philosophy at City University of New York. This means we are not actively aware of them unless they are extremely strong. But, low-level smells are still picked up because the scent receptors in our brain are so powerful that we unconsciously register them. In fact, various studies have found the olfactory bulb sends more neurons to more areas of our brain than our hearing or vision.

Research suggests that the power of smell can also affect how the brain performs, especially when it comes to the aroma of essential oils. Mark Moss, from the Department of Psychology at Northumbria University, found that sage and peppermint show general positive effects on cognition while the smell of rosemary can enhance our memory. He also investigated lavender which he says "tends to impair memory and slow down reaction time. But research by others have shown it to be useful in reducing pre-treatment anxiety in dental and medical situations".
So, don't take your nose for granted. It really is powerful!

vocabulary.entry: whiff /wɪf/ n. 一丝气味；一阵气味
vocabulary.example: I caught a whiff of fresh bread as I walked past the bakery.
vocabulary.translation: 我路过面包店时闻到了一丝新鲜面包的香味。

vocabulary.example: There are deep psychological reasons for his behaviour.
vocabulary.translation: 他的行为背后有深刻的心理原因。

vocabulary.example: Her personality made her very popular with her classmates.
vocabulary.translation: 她的性格让她在同学中很受欢迎。

vocabulary.entry: cognition /kɒɡˈnɪʃn/ n. 认知；认知能力
vocabulary.example: Reading helps to improve children's cognition.
vocabulary.translation: 阅读有助于提升儿童的认知能力。

vocabulary.example: The perfumer created a new fragrance for the brand.
vocabulary.translation: 这位调香师为该品牌调制了一款新香水。

vocabulary.example: The olfactory system is responsible for our sense of smell.
vocabulary.translation: 嗅觉系统负责我们的嗅觉感知。

vocabulary.example: The olfactory bulb processes information about smells.
vocabulary.translation: 嗅球处理气味相关信息。

vocabulary.entry: process /ˈprəʊses/ v. 处理（信息、感觉）
vocabulary.example: The brain processes information from the senses.
vocabulary.translation: 大脑处理来自感官的信息。

vocabulary.example: The room had a pleasant odour of flowers.
vocabulary.translation: 房间里弥漫着宜人的花香。

vocabulary.entry: unique /juˈniːk/ adj. 独特的；独一无二的
vocabulary.example: Everyone has a unique set of fingerprints.
vocabulary.translation: 每个人都有独一无二的指纹。

vocabulary.example: The word has strong associations with my childhood.
vocabulary.translation: 这个词让我产生强烈的童年联想。

vocabulary.example: There is a growing awareness of environmental issues.
vocabulary.translation: 人们对环境问题的意识日益增强。

vocabulary.entry: primarily /ˈpraɪmərəli/ adv. 主要地；根本地
vocabulary.example: The area is primarily residential.
vocabulary.translation: 这个区域主要是住宅区。

vocabulary.entry: unconscious /ʌnˈkɒnʃəs/ adj. 无意识的；潜意识的
vocabulary.example: He was unconscious of the effect he had on people.
vocabulary.translation: 他没意识到自己对他人的影响。

vocabulary.example: Receptors in the nose detect different smells.
vocabulary.translation: 鼻腔中的感受器能感知不同气味。

vocabulary.example: Her face registered surprise when she saw the gift.
vocabulary.translation: 看到礼物时，她脸上露出了惊讶的神情。

vocabulary.example: Neurons carry signals between the brain and the body.
vocabulary.translation: 神经元在大脑和身体之间传递信号。

vocabulary.example: Her vision was perfect until she was fifty.
vocabulary.translation: 她五十岁之前视力一直很好。

vocabulary.example: The aroma of coffee filled the room.
vocabulary.translation: 咖啡的香气弥漫了整个房间。

vocabulary.entry: essential /ɪˈsenʃl/ adj. 本质的；精油相关的
vocabulary.example: Many products use essential oils for their scent.
vocabulary.translation: 许多产品使用精油来增添香味。

vocabulary.example: Sage is used in cooking and herbal medicine.
vocabulary.translation: 鼠尾草可用于烹饪和草药。

vocabulary.example: Peppermint has a fresh, strong smell.
vocabulary.translation: 薄荷有着清新浓烈的气味。

vocabulary.example: Rosemary is often used to flavour meat dishes.
vocabulary.translation: 迷迭香常用来给肉类菜肴调味。

vocabulary.example: This drug will enhance your performance.
vocabulary.translation: 这种药物会提升你的表现。

vocabulary.example: Lavender is often used to help people sleep.
vocabulary.translation: 薰衣草常用来帮助人们睡眠。

vocabulary.example: Lack of sleep impairs your ability to think clearly.
vocabulary.translation: 睡眠不足会损害清晰思考的能力。

vocabulary.example: My first reaction was to say no.
vocabulary.translation: 我的第一反应是拒绝。

vocabulary.example: She suffers from anxiety before exams.
vocabulary.translation: 她考试前会感到焦虑。

vocabulary.entry: dental /ˈdentl/ adj. 牙科的；牙齿的
vocabulary.example: Regular dental check-ups are important.
vocabulary.translation: 定期牙科检查很重要。

vocabulary.entry: medical /ˈmedɪkl/ adj. 医疗的；医学的
vocabulary.example: He is seeking medical advice for his back pain.
vocabulary.translation: 他正在为背痛寻求医疗建议。
